scope: St Peter's Basilica, Vatican City (simplified schematic)
title: St Peter's Basilica
blurb: The Papal Basilica of Saint Peter in the Vatican in simplified schematic form: 220 m long, with the 136.6 m dome, the 114 m facade, the bronze baldachin and the embracing colonnade.

sourceUrls.label: Opus Dei: 400 Years of the Basilica of Saint Peter

systems.name: Facade and vestibule
systems.description: Maderno's 51 m high, 114 m wide facade with giant columns, five portals and thirteen attic statues, in simplified form.

systems.name: Nave and crossing
systems.description: The long nave with its barrel vault, the aisles, the four crossing piers and the chapel blocks.

systems.name: Transept and apse
systems.description: The 150 m wide transept and the semicircular apse with its conch.

systems.name: Dome
systems.description: Michelangelo's dome: drum, 42 m shell with sixteen ribs, and the lantern, ball and cross rising to 136.6 m.

systems.name: Baldachin
systems.description: Bernini's 28.5 m bronze canopy over the high altar.

systems.name: Colonnade
systems.description: Bernini's elliptical colonnade embracing St Peter's Square, in simplified form.

systems.name: Square and obelisk
systems.description: St Peter's Square with the Vatican obelisk and the two fountains.

explanations.facade block: The 51 m high, 114 m wide facade wall with its entablature and attic, merged into one mass. Exact articulation is schematic.
explanations.facade columns: The eight giant columns of the facade order, merged into one part. Exact diameters and heights are schematic.
explanations.facade portals: The five portals from the vestibule into the basilica, merged into one part: the Holy Door (northernmost, opened only for holy years), the central Filarete bronze door of 1455 and the Door of the Dead (southernmost) among them. Exact recesses are schematic.
explanations.attic statues: The thirteen colossal attic statues, merged into one part: Christ the Redeemer at the center with St John the Baptist and eleven apostles. Exact figures are schematic.
explanations.vestibule: The 71 m wide, 13.5 m deep, 28 m high entrance hall behind the facade, with its 28 m internal pilasters, merged into one part. Exact detail is schematic.
explanations.nave block: The nave walls and floor, merged into one part; the nave interior rises 46.2 m. Exact wall thicknesses are schematic.
explanations.nave vault: The barrel vault over the nave, the highest church vault of its kind. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.aisle blocks: The aisle blocks flanking the nave with their roofs, merged into one part. Exact widths are schematic.
explanations.crossing piers: The four gargantuan crossing piers, 73 m in circumference each, merged into one part; their niches hold the colossal statues of Longinus, Helena, Veronica and Andrew. Exact cross sections are schematic.
explanations.chapel blocks: The chapels off the aisles and the sacristy, merged into one part. Exact volumes and positions are schematic.
explanations.transept block: The 150 m wide transept with its end walls, roof and floor, merged into one part. Exact depth is schematic.
explanations.apse: The semicircular apse with its semi-dome conch at the west end, merged into one part. Exact radius is schematic.
explanations.dome drum: The drum of the dome, 190 m in circumference, 20 m high and rising to 73 m, with its plinth, cornice and sixteen windows, merged into one part. Exact detail is schematic.
explanations.dome shell: The dome shell, 42.0 m in outer diameter, the tallest dome in the world. Exact profile is schematic.
explanations.dome ribs: The sixteen ribs of the dome with their buttress fins, merged into one part. Exact cross sections are schematic.
explanations.lantern, ball and cross: The 19 m lantern, the 2.4 m ball and the 4.9 m cross, merged into one part; from the pavement to the top of the cross is 136.6 m. Exact subdivision is schematic.
explanations.baldachin columns: Bernini's four 11 m helical bronze columns on their pedestals, merged into one part; the twist is approximated by stacked offset rings. Exact ornament is schematic.
explanations.baldachin canopy: The entablature, volutes, orb and cross of the 28.5 m baldachin, merged into one part. Exact detail is schematic.
explanations.north arm columns: The columns of the north colonnade arm, part of the 284 columns of the colonnade, merged into one part. Exact count is schematic.
explanations.north arm entablature: The entablature, attic and pilasters of the north arm, merged into one part. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.north arm statues: The statues crowning the north arm, part of the 140 statues above the colonnade, merged into one part. Exact figures are schematic.
explanations.south arm columns: The columns of the south colonnade arm, part of the 284 columns of the colonnade, merged into one part. Exact count is schematic.
explanations.south arm entablature: The entablature, attic and pilasters of the south arm, merged into one part. Exact profiles are schematic.
explanations.south arm statues: The statues crowning the south arm, part of the 140 statues above the colonnade, merged into one part. Exact figures are schematic.
explanations.entrance corridors: The straight corridors linking the facade to the colonnade arms, merged into one part. Exact alignment is schematic.
explanations.obelisk: The Vatican obelisk, 25.5 m of shaft rising to 40 m with base and cross, merged into one part; moved to the square in 1586 under Sixtus V by Domenico Fontana. Exact pedestal form is schematic.
explanations.fountains: The two fountains of St Peter's Square, merged into one part. Exact forms are schematic.
explanations.square paving: The paving of St Peter's Square, shown schematically; the real square is 340 m long and 240 m wide. Exact extent and pattern are schematic.
